$comment: Single source of brand truth for every public asset. Nothing in site/ or docs/marketing/ may hardcode a name, domain or package scope: they read these tokens. The name was decided on 2026-08-07 (Accordo) and the code surface renamed with scripts/brand-set.js; the tokens remain the single edit point, because a trademark screen could still force a second rename.

name.note: Chosen by the founder on 2026-08-07 over Pactar (more distinctive, but a live PACT word-mark in class 9) and Pactio (a live UK legal-tech namesake in adjacent software). Research and the eliminated candidates are in docs/marketing/NAME_VERIFICATION.md. The trademark screen has NOT been run — if it comes back badly, scripts/brand-set.js runs again with a different name.

domain.note: Registered by the founder on 2026-08-07. The registrar showed it as unavailable in a check run minutes earlier, which is consistent with that purchase — a DNS lookup the same morning had shown no A record, and this field warned that DNS silence is not proof either way. Ownership is the founder's statement; this environment can confirm the domain is registered, not to whom.

repository.note: Public since 2026-08-08, confirmed against the GitHub API rather than assumed. Flipping this one field is what turns indexing on: meta robots, robots.txt, the sitemap reference, both calls to action, the status banner and the codeRepository property in the structured data all follow it. vercel.json drops X-Robots-Tag in the same commit, and scripts/site-check.js refuses to let the two disagree.

npm.note: The two unscoped names are held, the scope is not. `accordo@0.0.1` and `create-accordo@0.0.1` were published by the founder on 2026-08-09 as placeholders and confirmed against the registry here (HTTP 200, maintainer aetha-ai) rather than taken on trust; `@accordo/mcp` and `@accordo/core` still return 404, so the scope is unclaimed and server.json's identifier resolves to nothing. The source now scaffolds and the registry does not, and those are two different facts: `packages/create-accordo` became real code on 2026-08-09 (`projectBootstrapContract: 1`, proven by `tests/project-bootstrap.test.js`), and run from a checkout of this repository it writes a project that boots, reports `valid` from `app inspect` and exits 0 from `project doctor` — which is what `sourceScaffolds: true` above records. The published `create-accordo@0.0.1` tarball is unchanged and still empty, so `npm create accordo` fetches that placeholder and installs nothing. The true sentence is 'create-accordo scaffolds a working project from this repository'; '`npm create accordo` works today' stays false until a human publishes, and no document may say the second. `status` remains `names-reserved` because this field describes the registry rather than the repository, and it is what gates the MCP-registry submission. `packages/create-accordo/package.json` is `private: true` so that publishing stays a deliberate human act — scripts/distribution-check.js fails if that flag and this status ever disagree.

license.note: Confirmed by the founder on 2026-08-07 (ADR-023). MIT has been the repository licence since Milestone 0; what changed is that a distribution manifest may now assert it to a marketplace, which scripts/distribution-check.js refuses while the status is provisional.

promise: Describe your sales process to your coding agent; own the CRM it builds.
colorsNote: Inherited verbatim from apps/admin/public/styles.css so the site and the product it ships are visibly the same thing.

typography.sans: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif
